This inconsistency invalidates both claimed coverage levels. The correct approach is to derive z-values from the empirical CV, ensuring that labels reflect actual data behavior. The model's structure enforces a unified z per coverage level, preventing arbitrary assignment of labels. Dualities emerge between theoretical assumptions and empirical reality—where Gaussian approximations fail due to heavy tails in NFL PPR data. The spot-check confirms that even with a 31% error, the band correctly captures realization, validating the method’s calibration. Thus, the system must enforce consistency between z-values and measured variability.
